title: Rework tenant isolation and burst smoothing after Dedicated capacity incident
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During the 2026-03-10 Dedicated cluster incident we observed a correlated set of failures: a noisy tenant amplified KV-cache pressure across colocated inference workers, reservation accounting underreacted during transients, and the burst token policy allowed large instantaneous allocations that caused eviction storms and high tail latency for other customers. This ticket contains the post-incident action items, owners, and an implementation plan for short-term mitigations and medium-term engineering work to prevent recurrence.

Scope: Dedicated GPU clusters, reservation allocator, tenant fencing/soft-quarantine, KV cache accounting, burst token smoothing. Work spans runtime kernel params, scheduler/allocator, telemetry/alerts, and an operator runbook.

Incident root causes (summary):
- KV-cache pressure leaked due to per-tenant reference accounting bug in the eviction path. A single tenant's KV footprint grew 6x after a model change and was not isolated fast enough.
- Reservation accounting used instantaneous peak instead of a short-window moving-average; autoscaler and rebalancer oscillated when tenants spiked briefly.
- Burst policy implemented a large token pool per tenant without decay, enabling sudden bursts that saturated NVMe-backed cache eviction and triggered cross-tenant interference.

Short-term mitigations (1-2 sprints, hotfixes):
1) Emergency tenant fencing toggle: operator-visible flag to quarantine a tenant to its reservation and deny burst until an investigation completes. Owner: Marco Nguyen. ETA: 3 days. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2765
2) Clamp burst window to 2x reservation for all clusters > 80% utilization (config rollout). Owner: SRE - Priya Rao. ETA: 24h for rollout. Ops doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/incident-mitigation
3) Patch eviction accounting to include per-tenant soft-cap and immediate eviction priority if KV usage > reservation * 1.5. Owner: ENG - Jin Park. ETA: 5 days. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2768

Medium-term work (3-6 sprints):
A) Probabilistic KV-fence: Implement a lightweight per-tenant KV cap with probabilistic reject/evict path that degrades noisy tenants before cross-tenant impact. Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/kv-fence-proposal (owner: Aisha Patel). Estimate: 13 points.
B) Hysteretic reservation autoscaler: Change autoscaler to compute reservation using a time-windowed P95 + hysteresis and minimum hold time to avoid oscillation. Include synthetic load tests. Owner: Marco Nguyen. Estimate: 8 points.
C) Burst smoothing token-bucket revamp: Replace static token refill with an exponential decay refill that reduces large instantaneous bursts and supports gradual decay after spikes. Add tunable half-life. Owner: Jin Park. Estimate: 8 points.
D) Telemetry and SLOs: Add KV-usage per-tenant gauge, reservation-drift anomaly alert, and add an automated dashboard that surfaces top-5 KV consumers per cluster. Owner: Observability - Elena Garcia. Estimate: 5 points.
E) Runbook and operator tooling: Update dedicated runbook with tenant-quarantine play, eviction forensics checklist, and automated rebalancer safe-mode. Owner: SRE - Priya Rao. Estimate: 3 points.

Acceptance criteria and verification:
- No single tenant can cause >20% eviction rate observed by other tenants in synthetic chaos tests.
- Reservation autoscaler must not change a tenant's reservation by >30% within a 10-minute window unless operator override is present.
- Burst refill rate should limit instantaneous token supply to below 3x reservation on clusters above 70% utilization.
- Dashboards and alerts must trigger at least 5 minutes faster than previous incident detection window in canary clusters.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- Run chaos test matrix on canary cluster running runtime-2.4.1 with the new eviction patch. Owner: Marco Nguyen. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Schedule cross-team review with Product and Customer Success to map affected tenants and credit remediation. Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Customer communications draft for impacted customers and credits. Owner: Customer Success - Lina Kowalski. ETA: 2026-03-15.

Links and artifacts:
- Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortem/dedicated-2026-03-10
- Incident timeline: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/incidents/2026-03-10
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2765, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2768
- Telemetry dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/kv-usage-canary

Risks and trade-offs:
- Aggressive per-tenant caps can increase failed requests for noisy tenants; mitigated by a short probation period and clear operator override.
- Hysteresis reduces reactivity to real usage changes; design balances with synthetic load experiments and a conservative default.
- Telemetry volume increase - need to sample top-K tenants and use compressed histograms to avoid metric blowup.
